heading.b: Provisions consequent on enactment of Courts and Crimes Legislation Further Amendment Act 2010
Changes to the jurisdictional limit of the Court

block.txt: The amendment made to section 29 by the Courts and Crimes Legislation Further Amendment Act 2010 does not apply to proceedings instituted in the Court before the commencement of the amendment.

A provision of the 2005 Extended Leave Determination that could have been made as a condition of service determination if this Act, as amended by the Courts and Crimes Legislation Further Amendment Act 2010, had been in force at the time that it was made, is taken to have been, and to have always been, validly made under section 22 of the Local Courts Act 1982.

The 2005 Extended Leave Determination is taken to include, and to have always included, a provision to the effect that, on and from the date an election by a Magistrate to be paid an extended leave gratuity takes effect, any service by the Magistrate as a Magistrate or in the public sector service before that date is to be disregarded in determining the Magistrate’s entitlement to extended leave for service after that date.

Anything done in connection with the 2005 Extended Leave Determination that would have been validly done if the amendments made to this Act by the Courts and Crimes Legislation Further Amendment Act 2010 had been in force when it was done is taken to have been, and to have always been, validly done.

A Magistrate or former Magistrate who was paid an extended leave gratuity before the commencement of this clause may elect to have his or her pre-2002 extended leave entitlement reinstated in accordance with arrangements approved by the Minister.
As a precondition to reinstatement, the Magistrate or former Magistrate must repay the gratuity amount to the Minister.
The amount to be repaid is to be determined by the Minister on the basis of a reasonable estimate of the present day value of the extended leave gratuity paid to the Magistrate or former Magistrate.

On reinstatement, the Magistrate or former Magistrate is taken to have accrued, and to always have accrued, extended leave as if the Magistrate had never elected to be paid the extended leave gratuity.
Expressions used in this clause have the same meaning as they have in clause 9A of Schedule 1.
In this clause—

extended leave gratuity means a gratuity paid to a Magistrate on election under clause 2A of the Magistrates’ Leave and Related Conditions Determination as inserted by the 2005 Extended Leave Determination.
2005 Extended Leave Determination means the Magistrates’ Leave and Related Conditions Amendment (Extended Leave) Determination 2005 published in Gazette No 65 of 3.6.2005 at page 1923.

heading.b: Provision consequent on enactment of Local Court Amendment (Company Title Home Unit Disputes) Act 2013
Jurisdiction in company title home unit disputes

block.txt: Section 34A extends to any company title home unit dispute that involves or relates to conduct by an interested party that occurred before the commencement of that section.

heading.b: Provision consequent on enactment of Justice Portfolio Legislation (Miscellaneous Amendments) Act 2016

block.txt: Clause 12 (4) of Schedule 1, as in force before its substitution by the Justice Portfolio Legislation (Miscellaneous Amendments) Act 2016, continues to apply until the Statutory and Other Offices Remuneration Tribunal makes provision for the remuneration of acting Magistrates under the Statutory and Other Offices Remuneration Act 1975.

heading.b: Provision consequent on enactment of Justice Legislation Amendment Act (No 3) 2018

block.txt: The amendment made to section 29 by the Justice Legislation Amendment Act (No 3) 2018 does not apply to proceedings instituted in the Court before the commencement of the amendment.

heading.b: Provision consequent on enactment of Local Court Amendment (Jurisdiction) Act 2025

block.txt: If, immediately before the commencement, pending proceedings had been heard or partly heard, the pending proceedings may continue to be dealt with and determined by the Local Court as if the amendment Act had not commenced.
If, immediately before the commencement, pending proceedings had not commenced to be heard, from the commencement the pending proceedings are—
taken to have been commenced in the District Court, and
to be heard and determined in the District Court.
In this clause—
amendment Act means the Local Court Amendment (Jurisdiction) Act 2025.
commencement means the commencement of the amendment Act.

pending proceedings means proceedings for invasion of privacy or other privacy contravention, including proceedings for administrative review under the Privacy and Personal Information Protection Act 1998, section 55, commenced in the Local Court but not finalised.

heading.b: Provision consequent on enactment of Local Court and Bail Legislation Amendment Act 2025—bail amendments
Bail decisions made by registrar or authorised officer continue in force

block.txt: A decision made under section 65 by a registrar or authorised officer about bail that is in force immediately before the commencement continues in force as if the amendment Act had not commenced.
In this clause—
amendment Act means the Local Court and Bail Legislation Amendment Act 2025.
commencement means the commencement of the amendment Act, Schedule 3.

heading.b: Provisions consequent on enactment of Local Court and Bail Legislation Amendment Act 2025—new judicial offices

block.txt: In this part—
amending Act means the Local Court and Bail Legislation Amendment Act 2025.
commencement date means the date on which the amending Act, Schedules 1 and 2 commence.
former offices—see clause 23.
new offices means the following offices of the Local Court—
Chief Judge,
Deputy Chief Judge,
Judge.

heading.b: Abolition of offices of Chief Magistrate, Deputy Chief Magistrate and Magistrate

block.txt: The following offices of the Local Court (former offices) are abolished on the commencement date—
Chief Magistrate,
Deputy Chief Magistrate,
Magistrate.
See the Constitution Act 1902, section 56(2), which provides for the consequences of abolishing a judicial office.
On the commencement date—
the person holding office as the Chief Magistrate immediately before the abolition of the office is appointed as the Chief Judge of the Local Court, and
a person holding office as a Deputy Chief Magistrate immediately before the abolition of the office is appointed as a Deputy Chief Judge of the Local Court, and
a person holding office as a Magistrate immediately before the abolition of the office is appointed as a Judge of the Local Court, and
a person acting as a Magistrate immediately before the abolition of the office of Magistrate is appointed to act as a Judge of the Local Court.

A person referred to in subclause (1) is taken to hold the new office, or to act in the new office, subject to the terms and conditions, including remuneration, that applied to the person’s former office immediately before the commencement date.
A person referred to in subclause (1)(d) is appointed to act as a Judge for the remainder of the term for which the person was appointed to act as a Magistrate.
Unless the contrary intention appears, a person’s service in a former office must be reckoned for all purposes as service in the person’s new office corresponding to the former office.
To avoid doubt, the appointment under subclause (1) does not require a further commission under the public seal of the State.

heading.b: Abolition of former offices has no effect on proceedings

block.txt: A person appointed to a new office by clause 24 may continue to hear and determine or otherwise deal with proceedings that, immediately before the commencement date, were pending before or being heard by the person in the person’s capacity as the holder of a former office.
Schedule 1, clause 4 does not apply to the person.

heading.b: Continuing effect of things done before commencement of amending Act

block.txt: An act, matter or thing done under this Act, or another Act, by a person holding a former office immediately before the commencement date is taken to have been done by the person—
in the person’s capacity as the holder of the new office corresponding to the person’s former office, and
under this Act, or the other Act, as amended by the amending Act.

Forms approved by the Chief Magistrate under this Act, section 72 as in force before the commencement date are taken to have been approved by the Chief Judge under that section as amended by the amending Act.

heading.b: Continuation of positions relating to former offices

block.txt: This clause applies to a person who, immediately before the commencement date, holds a position, role or office (a relevant position) under this Act or another Act that the person is eligible to hold because the person holds, or has held, a former office.
The person continues to hold the relevant position despite—
the abolition of the person’s former office by clause 23, and
the amendments made to this Act or the other Act by the amending Act.
A person appointed to a new office by clause 24 is not required to take a judicial oath in relation to the new office to which the person is appointed.
In this clause—
judicial oath means the oath prescribed in the Oaths Act 1900, Fourth Schedule.

heading.b: Construction of references to retired office holders

block.txt: A relevant reference to a retired or former holder of a new office is taken to include a person who, immediately before the commencement date, is a retired or former holder of the corresponding former office.
In this clause—
corresponding former office means the following—
for the office of Chief Judge—the office of Chief Magistrate,
for the office of Deputy Chief Judge—the office of Deputy Chief Magistrate,
for the office of Judge—the office of Magistrate.
relevant reference means a reference in—
this Act or another Act, or
an instrument made under this Act or another Act.

heading.b: Construction of references to former offices

block.txt: Unless the contrary intention appears, a reference to a former office in this Act or another Act, other than the Constitution Act 1902, in an instrument made under this Act or another Act or in another document must be read as a reference to a new office as follows—
Chief Magistrate—Chief Judge,
Deputy Chief Magistrate—Deputy Chief Judge,
Magistrate—Judge,
acting Magistrate—acting Judge.
